name: EU AI Act Compliance Ruleset
description: Regulatory rules derived from Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the EU AI Act). Covers prohibited practices, high-risk requirements, transparency obligations, and GPAI obligations. Rules sourced from official EU texts and the EU AI Office.

rules.title: Risk management system
rules.description: A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained for high-risk AI systems. It shall consist of a continuous iterative process run throughout the entire lifecycle.
rules.evidence_guidance: Provide risk assessment documentation, risk register, mitigation plans, and evidence of periodic review.

rules.title: Known and foreseeable risks identification
rules.description: Identify the known and foreseeable risks the high-risk AI system can pose to health, safety or fundamental rights when used in accordance with its intended purpose.
rules.evidence_guidance: Provide a documented risk inventory with impact assessments for each identified risk.

rules.title: Foreseeable misuse analysis
rules.description: The risk management system must consider reasonably foreseeable misuse of the AI system.
rules.evidence_guidance: Provide misuse scenario analysis and mitigation strategies.

rules.title: Risk mitigation measures
rules.description: Adopt appropriate and targeted risk management measures to address identified risks.
rules.evidence_guidance: Show implemented mitigation controls for each identified risk.

rules.title: Residual risk assessment
rules.description: Assess whether residual risks remain acceptable after mitigation, with testing evidence.
rules.evidence_guidance: Document residual risk levels and justification for acceptability.

rules.title: Data governance for training, validation and testing
rules.description: Training, validation and testing datasets shall be subject to data governance practices appropriate for the intended purpose.
rules.evidence_guidance: Dataset documentation, provenance records, collection methodology.

rules.title: Dataset relevance and representativeness
rules.description: Datasets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible free of errors and complete.
rules.evidence_guidance: Dataset statistics, distribution analysis, representativeness assessment.

rules.title: Examination for biases
rules.description: Datasets shall be examined for possible biases likely to affect health and safety, negatively impact fundamental rights, or lead to discrimination.
rules.evidence_guidance: Bias testing results, fairness metrics, remediation actions.

rules.title: Data provenance and lineage
rules.description: Document the provenance of datasets used, including collection methods, origin, and processing history.
rules.evidence_guidance: Data lineage records, collection purpose documentation.

rules.title: Data minimisation and purpose limitation
rules.description: Data collection should be adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary for the intended purpose.
rules.evidence_guidance: Document data minimisation measures, retention policies.

rules.title: Technical documentation
rules.description: Draw up technical documentation before the system is placed on the market or put into service, kept up-to-date.
rules.evidence_guidance: Complete technical documentation per Annex IV requirements.

rules.title: System purpose and intended use
rules.description: Document the intended purpose, the provider, and the version of the AI system.
rules.evidence_guidance: Clear statement of intended purpose, version history, provider details.

rules.title: Architecture and design description
rules.description: Describe the system architecture, design specifications, and algorithms.
rules.evidence_guidance: Architecture diagrams, component descriptions, model/provider details.

rules.title: System limitations and known risks
rules.description: Document the known limitations, known risks, and foreseeable unintended outcomes.
rules.evidence_guidance: Limitations register, risk catalogue.

rules.title: Record-keeping (logging)
rules.description: High-risk AI systems shall enable the automatic recording of events (logs) over the system's lifetime.
rules.evidence_guidance: Logging implementation, log schema, retention configuration.

rules.title: Input/output traceability
rules.description: Logs shall record the inputs and outputs of the AI system, enabling traceability of decisions.
rules.evidence_guidance: Evidence of input/output logging with timestamps.

rules.title: Automatically generated logs
rules.description: Providers shall keep automatically generated logs for a period appropriate to the intended purpose (at least 6 months).
rules.evidence_guidance: Log retention policy, log storage evidence.

rules.title: Failure and error logging
rules.description: Log system failures, errors, and anomalous behavior for post-market monitoring.
rules.evidence_guidance: Error/failure log schema, incident logging implementation.

rules.title: User/session identity where appropriate
rules.description: Logs shall, where appropriate, identify the natural person who verified or overrode system outputs.
rules.evidence_guidance: Operator identification in logs.

rules.title: Human oversight capability
rules.description: High-risk AI systems shall be designed so they can be effectively overseen by natural persons.
rules.evidence_guidance: Human oversight implementation design, HMI tools, oversight procedures.

rules.title: Understanding system capabilities and limitations
rules.description: Overseers must be able to properly understand the capabilities and limitations of the high-risk AI system.
rules.evidence_guidance: Training materials, capability documentation, limitation disclosures.

rules.title: Override and stop capability
rules.description: Overseers must be able to decide not to use the system, disregard, override or reverse its output, or stop the system.
rules.evidence_guidance: Override mechanism implementation, stop/disable capability.

rules.title: Avoiding over-reliance (automation bias)
rules.description: Overseers must be able to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output.
rules.evidence_guidance: Automation bias mitigation training, UI design decisions.

rules.title: Human approval gates for consequential decisions
rules.description: For high-risk systems making decisions with significant impact on individuals, human approval should be required before action execution.
rules.evidence_guidance: Approval gate implementation, decision log with human sign-off.

rules.title: Appropriate level of accuracy
rules.description: High-risk AI systems shall achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, declared in the instructions for use.
rules.evidence_guidance: Accuracy metrics, evaluation methodology, benchmark results.

rules.title: Robustness and resilience
rules.description: Systems shall be resilient to errors, faults, inconsistencies, and adversarial manipulation.
rules.evidence_guidance: Robustness testing results, adversarial testing, error handling.

rules.title: Fallback plans and fail-safe behavior
rules.description: System shall have fallback plans in case of failure and default to a safe state.
rules.evidence_guidance: Fallback procedures, fail-safe implementation.

rules.title: Bias mitigation and fairness
rules.description: Systems shall be designed to reduce the risk of biased outputs, especially regarding sensitive attributes.
rules.evidence_guidance: Fairness metrics, bias testing across protected groups.

rules.title: Confidence thresholds and uncertainty handling
rules.description: System should use confidence thresholds and handle uncertainty appropriately, especially for consequential decisions.
rules.evidence_guidance: Confidence threshold configuration, uncertainty handling logic.

rules.title: Cybersecurity protections
rules.description: Systems shall be protected against attempts to alter their use, behaviour or performance by third parties exploiting vulnerabilities.
rules.evidence_guidance: Security architecture, threat model, penetration testing results.

rules.title: Authentication and authorization
rules.description: Implement strong authentication and authorization controls for system access and actions.
rules.evidence_guidance: Auth implementation details, access control configuration.

rules.title: Secret and credential management
rules.description: API keys, secrets, and credentials shall be managed securely, never in plaintext or source code.
rules.evidence_guidance: Secrets manager usage, no hardcoded secrets in codebase.

rules.title: Prompt injection and adversarial input mitigations
rules.description: Implement protections against prompt injection, adversarial inputs, and model manipulation.
rules.evidence_guidance: Input validation, sanitization, prompt injection testing.

rules.title: Tool permission boundaries and isolation
rules.description: Agent tools shall have appropriate permission boundaries and isolation between components.
rules.evidence_guidance: Tool permission configuration, sandbox evidence.

rules.title: Rate limiting and abuse prevention
rules.description: Implement rate limiting to prevent abuse and denial of service.
rules.evidence_guidance: Rate limiter configuration, abuse monitoring.

rules.title: User awareness of AI interaction
rules.description: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed in a way that those persons are informed they are interacting with AI.
rules.evidence_guidance: AI disclosure mechanism, user notification implementation.

rules.title: AI-generated content disclosure
rules.description: Outputs of AI systems that generate synthetic content shall be marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated.
rules.evidence_guidance: Content watermarking or labeling implementation.

rules.title: Explainability and interpretability
rules.description: Provide meaningful information about the logic involved in AI system outputs, enabling interpretation by affected persons.
rules.evidence_guidance: Model cards, explanation interfaces, interpretability documentation.

rules.title: Deepfake and synthetic content handling
rules.description: If the system generates or manipulates content resembling real persons or events, disclose this clearly.
rules.evidence_guidance: Synthetic content labeling policy and implementation.

rules.title: Accountable owner and quality management
rules.description: Designate an accountable person or team responsible for AI system compliance and establish a quality management system.
rules.evidence_guidance: Organizational chart, named responsible person, QMS documentation.

rules.title: AI system inventory and model registry
rules.description: Maintain an inventory of AI systems with versions, models, providers, and risk classifications.
rules.evidence_guidance: AI system inventory/documentation.

rules.title: Change management and version control
rules.description: Manage changes to the AI system through a documented change management process.
rules.evidence_guidance: Change log, version control, release management process.

rules.title: Incident response plan
rules.description: Establish and document an incident response procedure for AI system failures or serious incidents.
rules.evidence_guidance: Incident response plan document, reporting procedures.

rules.title: Post-market monitoring
rules.description: Establish and document a post-market monitoring system to collect and analyze performance data throughout the system lifetime.
rules.evidence_guidance: Post-market monitoring plan, monitoring data collection.

rules.title: Internal compliance review process
rules.description: Establish a periodic review process to assess ongoing compliance with the AI Act obligations.
rules.evidence_guidance: Compliance review schedule and records.
